Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

No card is a parcel.

All cards are envelopes.

Some envelopes are bags.

∴ Here, Only conclusion I follows.

Hence, "Option 1" is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which article has a similar provision to that of Article 32 and deals with writ jurisdiction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 226**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 226** of the Indian Constitution empowers the High Courts to issue certain writs.
 
• This Article extends the writ jurisdiction to all cases where a fundamental right is violated, as well as other legal rights.
 
• Article 226 can be invoked not only for the enforcement of fundamental rights but also for any other purpose.
 
• The power conferred by Article 226 is wider in scope as compared to Article 32, which is restricted to the enforcement of Fundamental Rights only.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 32**

 
 
• Article 32 of the Indian Constitution provides the right to constitutional remedies, allowing individuals to move the Supreme Court directly in case of violation of fundamental rights.
 
• It is known as the "heart and soul" of the Constitution as described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
 
• The Supreme Court can issue writs like habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari for the enforcement of fundamental rights.
 
• This Article is a crucial provision for the protection of Fundamental Rights in India.
 
 
 
• **Writs**
 
 
• A writ is a formal written order issued by a court.
 
• Types of writs include habeas corpus (to produce the body), mandamus (to command), prohibition (to forbid), quo warranto (by what authority), and certiorari (to be informed).
 
• These writs are powerful tools in the hands of the judiciary to ensure the protection of rights and to enforce public duties.
 
 
 
• **High Courts**
 
 
• High Courts are the principal civil courts of original jurisdiction in each state and union territory.
 
• They also have appellate jurisdiction over the subordinate courts.
 
• High Courts have the power to issue writs under Article 226 for the enforcement of fundamental rights and for other purposes.
 
• Their jurisdiction is broader compared to the Supreme Court in terms of issuing writs.

questions.question: Who among the following formed the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha in 1929?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swami Sahajanand Saraswati**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Swami Sahajanand Saraswati was a prominent peasant leader in India and was deeply involved in the peasant movement.
 
• He founded the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha (BPKS) in 1929 to address the issues of peasants and farmers in Bihar.
 
• The BPKS played a crucial role in mobilizing peasants against the zamindari system and for the rights of tenant farmers.
 
• Swami Sahajanand Saraswati later became the president of the All India Kisan Sabha, a nationwide peasant organization, further amplifying his influence in the peasant movement in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Peasant Movement in India:**

 
 
• The peasant movement in India was a series of political movements for the rights of the agricultural workers and against the feudal land system.
 
• These movements were significant in shaping the agrarian policies of the country and addressing issues like land reforms, tenancy rights, and fair wages.
 
 
 
• **Zamindari System:**
 
 
• The Zamindari system was a traditional land revenue system in India where landlords or zamindars collected rent from the peasants and paid a portion to the British colonial government.
 
• This system led to the exploitation of peasants, high rents, and forced labor, causing widespread agrarian distress.
 
 
 
• **All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS):**
 
 
• The AIKS was formed in 1936 as a national organization to address the issues faced by peasants across India.
 
• It worked towards the abolition of the zamindari system, fair land distribution, and better living conditions for agricultural workers.
 
 
 
• **Swami Sahajanand Saraswati's Contributions:**
 
 
• He was a key figure in the peasant movement and worked tirelessly for the upliftment of the agrarian community.
 
• His efforts led to significant reforms in the agrarian sector, and he is remembered as a champion of peasant rights in India.

questions.question: Who founded the Prarthana Samaj in Mumbai in 1867?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atmaram Pandurang**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Atmaram Pandurang was a social reformer and the founder of the **Prarthana Samaj in Mumbai in 1867.**
 
• The Prarthana Samaj was a movement for religious and social reform in Maharashtra based on earlier reform movements.
 
• The organization aimed to make people believe in one God and discard the caste system and superstitions.
 
• Atmaram Pandurang's efforts were directed towards promoting women's education and widow remarriage and opposing child marriage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prarthana Samaj**

 
 
• Prarthana Samaj was inspired by the Brahmo Samaj founded by** Raja Ram Mohan Roy in Bengal.**
 
• It was established by Atmaram Pandurang in 1867 to reform the social practices and religious beliefs of the Hindus in Maharashtra.
 
• The Samaj's principles were based on the teachings of Christianity and the ancient Hindu scriptures, advocating monotheism and discarding idol worship.
 
• Prominent members of the Prarthana Samaj included Justice** Mahadev Govind Ranade, R.G. Bhandarkar, and N.G. Chandavarkar**, who played significant roles in the social reform movements in Maharashtra.
 
 
 
• **Brahmo Samaj**
 
 
• Founded by **Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828 in Kolkata,** Brahmo Samaj was one of the earliest reform movements in India.
 
• The Samaj aimed at purifying Hinduism and promoting monotheism, rejecting the caste system, idol worship, and rituals.

• **Basicity:**

 
 
• Basicity refers to the ability of a substance to accept protons (H+ ions) or donate a pair of valence electrons to form a bond.
 
• In the context of alkali metal hydroxides, basicity is determined by the extent to which the hydroxide ion (OH-) is available to react with acids.
 
 
 
• **Alkali Metal Hydroxides:**
 
 
• Alkali metal hydroxides are compounds formed by alkali metals (Group 1 elements) and hydroxide ions (OH-).

• **Ionic Nature:**
 
 
• The ionic nature of a compound refers to the extent to which it dissociates into ions in a solution.
 
• Alkali metal hydroxides dissociate completely in water, releasing hydroxide ions, which contribute to their basicity.

questions.question: When the analysis of population density is done by calculating it through net cultivated area, then the measure is termed as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Physiological density**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Physiological density is a measure of population density that refers to the number of people per unit area of arable land.
 
• This measure provides insights into the pressure exerted by the population on the productive land area.
 
• It helps in understanding the carrying capacity of the land and the potential challenges in terms of food production and resource management.
 
• Physiological density is considered more meaningful than simple population density (people per total land area) because it focuses on the land that can actually support human life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agricultural Density**

 
 
• Agricultural density is a measure of the number of farmers per unit area of arable land.
 
• This metric helps in understanding the agricultural efficiency and the potential output of the farming sector.
 
• It provides insights into the level of development and technological advancement in agriculture within a region.
 
• Higher agricultural density may indicate less mechanization and more labor-intensive agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Gross Density**
 
 
• Gross density refers to the total population divided by the total land area.
 
• This measure does not differentiate between arable and non-arable land, giving an overall view of population distribution.
 
• It is useful for general demographic studies and urban planning purposes.
 
• However, it may not accurately reflect the actual human impact on the productive land resources.
 
 
 
• **Net Density**
 
 
• Net density is a less commonly used term and is not a standard measure in population geography.
 
• It might refer to a refined measure of population density considering specific criteria or exclusions.
 
• In most contexts, "net density" is not clearly defined or widely recognized.
 
• It is important to refer to more standardized measures like physiological or agricultural density for accurate analysis.

__
 
• **Monoecious plants** have both male (androecium) and female (gynoecium) reproductive organs in the same plant.
 
• This characteristic allows monoecious plants to self-pollinate, although cross-pollination can also occur.
 
• Examples of monoecious plants include maize, cucumbers, and squash.
 
• Monoecious plants are different from dioecious plants, which have male and female reproductive organs on separate plants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The androecium is the male reproductive part of a flower.
 
• It consists of stamens, each of which has a filament topped by an anther where pollen is produced.
 
 
 
• **Gynoecium**
 
 
• The gynoecium is the female reproductive part of a flower.
 
• It consists of one or more carpels, each containing an ovary, style, and stigma.
 
• The ovary contains ovules, which develop into seeds upon fertilization.
 
 
 
• **Dioecious**
 
 
• Dioecious plants have male and female reproductive organs on separate plants.
 
• This means that a dioecious plant is either male or female, not both.
 
• Examples of dioecious plants include holly, willow, and asparagus.

• Self-pollination occurs within the same flower or plant, while cross-pollination occurs between different plants.

questions.question: Which of the following decomposition reactions is NOT a redox reaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Decomposition of calcium carbonate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The decomposition of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) results in the formation of calcium oxide (CaO) and carbon dioxide (CO₂).
 
• This reaction is represented by the equation: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂.
 
• The oxidation states of the elements do not change during this decomposition reaction, indicating it is not a redox reaction.
 
• In contrast, decomposition reactions that are redox reactions involve changes in the oxidation states of the participating elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decomposition Reactions**

 
 
• A decomposition reaction is a type of chemical reaction in which a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler compounds or elements.
 
• These reactions often require an input of energy in the form of heat, light, or electricity.
 
• Examples include the decomposition of water into hydrogen and oxygen (2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂) and the decomposition of potassium chlorate into potassium chloride and oxygen (2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂).
 
 
 
• **Redox Reactions**
 
 
• Redox reactions, or oxidation-reduction reactions, involve the transfer of electrons between two substances.
 
• Oxidation refers to the loss of electrons, while reduction refers to the gain of electrons.
 
• In a redox reaction, one substance is oxidized (loses electrons) and another is reduced (gains electrons).
 
• An example is the decomposition of sodium hydride (NaH), where NaH decomposes into sodium metal (Na) and hydrogen gas (H₂), with sodium being reduced and hydrogen being oxidized.
 
 
 
• **Oxidation States**
 
 
• The oxidation state (or number) of an element in a compound is a measure of the degree of oxidation of that element.
 
• It is defined as the charge an atom would have if all bonds were completely ionic.
 
• Changes in oxidation states during a reaction indicate a redox process.

questions.question:
Simplify:

(x³ + 15x² + 75x + 125)/(x² - 25) (x - 5).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Recognize the numerator x³ + 15x² + 75x + 125 as the perfect cube (x + 5)³.

Recognize the denominator x² − 25 as the difference of squares (x − 5)(x + 5).

Expression becomes: [ (x + 5)³ ÷ ((x − 5)(x + 5)) ] × (x − 5).

Canceling common terms (x − 5) and (x + 5) yields (x + 5)².

Expanding (x + 5)² gives x² + 10x + 25.

**∴ The correct answer is x² + 10x + 25.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: (x³ + 15x² + 75x + 125) / (x² − 25) × (x − 5)

**Formula Used:**

1. (a + b)³ = a³ + 3a²b + 3ab² + b³

2. a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)

3. (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let us factorise the numerator: x³ + 15x² + 75x + 125

⇒ Numerator = (x)³ + 3(x)²(5) + 3(x)(5)² + (5)³ = (x + 5)³

⇒ Factorise the denominator: x² − 25 = (x)² − (5)² = (x − 5)(x + 5)

⇒ Substitute these into the given expression:

⇒ [ (x + 5)³ / ( (x − 5)(x + 5) ) ] × (x − 5)

⇒ Cancel out the common factor (x − 5) from the numerator multiplier and denominator.

⇒ The expression simplifies to: (x + 5)³ / (x + 5)

⇒ Cancel out one (x + 5) term to get: (x + 5)²

⇒ Expand using the formula (a + b)²:

⇒ (x + 5)² = x² + 2(x)(5) + 5² = x² + 10x + 25

**∴ The correct answer is x² + 10x + 25.**

**__Additional Information__**

Cubic Identities

Formulas for the sum and difference of cubes: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) and a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

Perfect Cube Expansions

Expanded forms: (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b) and (a − b)³ = a³ − b³ − 3ab(a − b).

Simplification of Rational Expressions

Always factorise both the numerator and the denominator into their simplest forms before attempting to cancel common terms.
</p

questions.question: Which of the following can be the value of k, if ((88 div 8 times k - 3 times 3))/((6² - 7 times 5 + k²)) = 1

Solve the given expression directly using the BODMAS rule:

⇒ (11k − 9) ÷ (36 − 35 + k²) = 1

⇒ (11k − 9) = (1 + k²)

⇒ k² − 11k + 10 = 0

⇒ (k − 10)(k − 1) = 0 ⇒ k = 1, 10

**∴ The correct answer is 1, 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(88 ÷ 8 × k − 3 × 3) / (6² − 7 × 5 + k²) = 1

**Method Used:**

According to the BODMAS rule, perform division first, then multiplication, addition, and subtraction sequentially.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Step 1: Simplify the Numerator

⇒ Numerator = 88 ÷ 8 × k − 3 × 3

⇒ Numerator = 11 × k − 9 = 11k − 9

⇒ Step 2: Simplify the Denominator

⇒ Denominator = 6² − 7 × 5 + k²

⇒ Denominator = 36 − 35 + k² = 1 + k²

⇒ Step 3: Substitute both simplified values back into the equation

⇒ (11k − 9) / (1 + k²) = 1

⇒ 11k − 9 = 1 + k²

⇒ k² − 11k + 10 = 0

⇒ k² − 10k − k + 10 = 0

⇒ k(k − 10) − 1(k − 10) = 0

⇒ (k − 1)(k − 10) = 0

⇒ k = 1 or k = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 1, 10.**

BODMAS Rule

It dictates the correct order of mathematical operations: Brackets, Orders (powers/roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

Quadratic Equation Roots

For the standard quadratic equation form ax² + bx + c = 0, the Sum of the roots = −b/a and the Product of the roots = c/a.

The nature of roots is determined by the Discriminant (D = b² − 4ac). If D > 0, roots are real and distinct. If D = 0, roots are real and equal. If D < 0, roots are imaginary.

The candidate who got 59.375% of the valid votes cast was declared elected by 2484 votes. If the number of people eligible to vote in that election was 16,000, what is the value of y?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Winner gets 59.375% (19/32) and loser gets 40.625% (13/32) of valid votes.

Difference = 19/32 − 13/32 = 3/16 of valid votes = 2484.

Total valid votes = 2484 × 16/3 = 13248.

Total valid votes = Total Voters × (100 − y)% × 90%.

16000 × ((100 − y)/100) × (90/100) = 13248 ⇒ 144 × (100 − y) = 13248 ⇒ 100 − y = 92 ⇒ y = 8.

**∴ The correct answer is y = 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b2c44af52608f70f39502c7ad17e413664764ff64e31d6a43b6df8f3a543575d.png] 

⇒ Let total eligible voters = 16,000

⇒ Total votes cast = 16,000 × ((100 − y)/100)

⇒ Total valid votes = 16,000 × ((100 − y)/100) × (90/100) = 144 × (100 − y)

⇒ Winner's share of valid votes = 59.375% = 59375/100000 = 19/32

⇒ Loser's share of valid votes = 100% − 59.375% = 40.625% = 13/32

⇒ Majority difference = 19/32 − 13/32 = 6/32 = 3/16

⇒ Majority votes = (3/16) × Valid votes = 2484

⇒ Valid votes = 2484 × (16/3) = 828 × 16 = 13,248

⇒ Equating the valid votes: 144 × (100 − y) = 13,248

⇒ 100 − y = 13,248 ÷ 144

⇒ 100 − y = 92

⇒ y = 8

**∴ The correct answer is y = 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Valid vs Total Votes

In election problems, always calculate winning margins based on the correct base specified in the question. Total valid votes = Total votes cast − Invalid votes.

Successive Percentage Change

When consecutive filtering steps occur (e.g., people not voting, then invalid votes), chain the multiplying factors: Final = Initial × (1 − R₁/100) × (1 − R₂/100).

Fraction to Percentage Conversions

Memorizing eighths and sixteenths speeds up calculations: 1/16 = 6.25%, 3/16 = 18.75%, and 1/32 = 3.125%. Thus, 59.375% = 50% + 9.375% = 1/2 + 3/32 = 19/32.

questions.question:
Simplify:

((x² - 9))/(x + 3)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The given expression is in the form of (a² − b²) / (a + b).

We know the algebraic identity a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b).

Substituting x for a and 3 for b, the numerator breaks down to (x − 3)(x + 3).

Dividing by the denominator (x + 3), the common term cancels out entirely.

This leaves exactly (x − 3).

**∴ The correct answer is x − 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: (x² − 9) / (x + 3)

**Formula Used:**

Difference of squares: a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)

**Calculations:**

⇒ (x² − 9) / (x + 3)

⇒ (x² − 3²) / (x + 3)

⇒ Expand the numerator using the formula:

⇒ [(x − 3)(x + 3)] / (x + 3)

⇒ Cancel the common factor (x + 3) from both the numerator and the denominator:

⇒ x − 3

**∴ The correct answer is x − 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference of Squares

This is one of the most frequently used identities in algebraic simplification: a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b).

Perfect Square Trinomials

For standard expansions: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b².

Sum and Difference of Cubes

Higher power factorization formulas: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) and a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

Simplification Rules

Always factorize algebraic numerators and denominators to their simplest forms before attempting to cancel or cross-multiply terms.
</p

questions.question: Rajesh, in his printing press, got an order to print some books, out of which he completed (17)/(27) of the order in 34 days. In how many days did he complete the entire order of printing?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In the fraction 17/27, the denominator represents the total work and the numerator represents the completed work.

17 units of work take = 34 days

1 unit of work takes = 34 ÷ 17 = 2 days

Total work (27 units) takes = 27 × 2 = 54 days

**∴ The correct answer is 54 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Fraction of the order completed = 17/27

Time taken to complete this fraction of the order = 34 days

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1bf21276ede7d97d70373e49014b63c996e17c440423f07cc31ab41666943fca.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Total Time = Time taken for partial work ÷ Fraction of work completed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the number of days required to complete the entire order be x days.

⇒ Complete order is considered as 1 whole unit of work.

⇒ As per the given data, 17/27 of the work is completed in 34 days.

⇒ (17/27) × x = 34

⇒ x = 34 × (27/17)

⇒ x = 2 × 27

⇒ x = 54 days

**∴ The correct answer is 54 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unitary Method

It involves finding the value of a single unit and then multiplying that unit value by the required number of units to find the total value.

Work and Time Relationship

Work done is directly proportional to the time taken (assuming constant efficiency). If a fraction of work W is completed in T days, the entire work is completed in T ÷ W days.

Fraction to Whole Conversion

The denominator of a fraction generally represents the total parts, and the numerator represents the considered parts. Equating these parts directly to the given values leads to much faster calculations.
</p

questions.question: A grocer professes to sell rice at the cost price, but uses a fake weight of 870 g for 1 kg. Find his profit percentage (correct to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In dishonest dealer problems where goods are sold at cost price, the profit comes entirely from the false weight.

**Profit % = [(True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight] × 100**

Here, True Weight = 1000 g and False Weight = 870 g.

Profit % = [(1000 − 870) ÷ 870] × 100

Profit % = (130 ÷ 870) × 100 = (1300 ÷ 87)% ≈ 14.94%

**∴ The correct answer is 14.94%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Professed Selling Price = Cost Price

True weight for 1 kg = 1000 g

False weight used by the grocer = 870 g

**Formula Used:**

Profit % = [(Error) ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100

Profit % = [(Selling Price − Cost Price) ÷ Cost Price] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7343497ecc525a56ffc3893980e10d6ae118635b27dce66a03a812e8665a7d7a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the cost price of 1 g of rice be ₹1.

⇒ Selling Price charged to the customer (for 1000 g) = ₹1000.

⇒ Actual Cost Price incurred by the grocer (for providing 870 g) = ₹870.

⇒ Profit = Selling Price − Cost Price

⇒ Profit = 1000 − 870 = ₹130

⇒ Profit Percentage = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = (130 ÷ 870) × 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = (1300 ÷ 87)% ≈ 14.942%

⇒ Rounding off to two decimal places, we get 14.94%.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.94%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer (Selling at CP)

When a dealer professes to sell items at Cost Price but uses a false weight, his profit percentage is given strictly by the error in weight over the false weight given: Profit % = [Error ÷ (True Weight − Error)] × 100.

Dishonest Dealer (Selling at Profit/Loss)

If the dealer marks up his goods by x% and also uses a false weight, the effective profit is determined using a multiplying factor: Final SP/CP ratio = [(100 + x) / 100] × [True Weight / False Weight].

Fraud During Purchasing & Selling

If a dealer cheats by x% while buying (takes more) and y% while selling (gives less), his overall profit percentage is calculated effectively by taking the ratio of the quantities exchanged: [(100 + x) ÷ (100 − y) − 1] × 100.
